title: Catch the crash
hook: Stop bad input from crashing your program, and ask again until it is right.

warmup.q: A function only prints its answer and has no return. What does `x = f()` store in x?
warmup.explain: No return means the function hands back None. The printing happened, but nothing was handed back.
split cuts text at every comma and gives you a list of the pieces.

warmup.q: What type of thing does `input()` always give you?
warmup.explain: input() always gives text, even if the person types digits. Use int() or float() to convert.

why.heading: Crashes cost you
why.text: You ask for hours worked. Someone types `eight` instead of `8`. `int("eight")` fails, the program stops dead and shows a red error. Real people type the wrong thing all the time. A good tool does not die. It says "numbers only" and carries on, like a crew that fixes a problem without stopping the whole shoot.

why.heading: try and except
why.text:
`try:`
`    n = int(text)`
`except ValueError:`
`    print("Numbers only")`

Python **tries** the indented lines. If a ValueError happens, it jumps to the `except` lines instead of crashing. If nothing goes wrong, the `except` part is skipped.

why.heading: Name the error you expect
why.text: The word after `except` is the error you are ready for. **ValueError** is the right kind of thing with the wrong content, like `int("eight")`. **ZeroDivisionError** means you divided by zero. Naming the error matters: a different bug will still show up so you can fix it, instead of being hidden.

why.heading: Ask again until it is right
why.text: Put `try` inside `while True:` and add `break` after the line that worked. The loop runs forever, but `break` is only reached when the conversion worked, so it leaves the loop. If it fails, the `except` runs, the loop goes round, and Python asks again. Like a 1st AD calling "going again!" until the take is good.

why.heading: Stack several excepts
why.text:
You can put more than one `except` under one `try`. Python picks the one that matches:

`except ValueError:`
`    print("Numbers only")`
`except ZeroDivisionError:`
`    print("Cannot divide by 0")`

Pace is minutes divided by km. If km is 0, it crashes. Nobody can run zero km.

watch.intro: The lesson types `eight` and then `8` for you. Watch the program ask again.
explain: `int(text)` fails on `eight`, so Python jumps to `except ValueError` and prints the message.
The `break` was skipped, so the loop goes round and asks again.
On `8` the conversion works, `break` leaves the loop, and the pay is shown.
watch.break_it: Now break it: change `ValueError` to `ZeroDivisionError` and tap Run. The error is now a plain `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'eight'`. That means: your except waited for a different error, so this one got through. The name after except must match. Put it back.

tasks.title: Fill in the error name
tasks.task: The program asks for km. If it is a number it shows `Got 10`. If not it must show `Not a number`. The blank `___` is where the error name goes. Replace it.
hints: The blank is the name of the error that int("ten") causes.

tasks.title: Ask again until valid
tasks.task: Ask `Hours? ` until a whole number is typed. For each bad answer show `Try again`. Then show the pay at R150 an hour, like `Pay: R1200` for 8 hours.
tasks.starter:
while True:
    text = input("Hours? ")
    # try to turn text into a whole number called hours
    # if it works, break. If it fails, print Try again

print(f"Pay: R{hours * 150}")
hints: Inside the loop you need a try, then an except ValueError.
In the try: hours = int(text) and then break. In the except: print("Try again").
try: on its own line, then indented hours = int(text) and break. Then except ValueError: and print("Try again"), lined up with try.

tests.expect:
Hours? abc
Try again
Hours? 8
Pay: R1200

Hours? x
Try again
Hours? y
Try again
Hours? 10
Pay: R1500

tasks.title: Safe pace
tasks.task: The pace program crashes on bad input. Wrap it in one `try`. Show `Numbers only` for a ValueError and `Km cannot be 0` for a ZeroDivisionError. Good input still shows the pace, like `6.00 min per km`.
tasks.starter:
minutes = int(input("Minutes? "))
km = int(input("Km? "))
print(f"{minutes / km:.2f} min per km")
hints: Put the three lines inside a try, indented by 4 spaces. Then add two except blocks.
except ValueError: prints Numbers only. except ZeroDivisionError: prints Km cannot be 0.
The two except lines are lined up with the word try, not indented.

recap: `try:` runs risky lines. `except ErrorName:` runs if that error happens.
Name the error you expect. ValueError for bad conversions, ZeroDivisionError for dividing by 0.
`while True` plus `try` plus `break` asks again until the answer is valid.
You can stack several `except` blocks under one `try`.

words.meaning: Run these lines, and be ready if one fails.
What to do if the named error happens.
Right kind of thing, wrong content, like int("eight").
You tried to divide by zero.
